title: A Cricketer Beat Shah Rukh Khan to India's Most Valuable Celebrity. And the Only Woman in the Top Three Hasn't Made a Hindi Film in Seven Years.
excerpt: Fortune India's first-ever Most Valuable Celebrities list put Virat Kohli, Shah Rukh Khan and Priyanka Chopra Jonas on three standalone covers. Look closer and the rankings tell you exactly where star power lives in 2026 — and it isn't only the movies.
body:
Three faces, three covers, one quiet power shift. Fortune India, in partnership with global brand consultancy Interbrand India, has published its maiden Most Valuable Celebrities ranking for 2026 — and the first thing you notice is who's on the cover and who isn't.

At number one: not a movie star at all, but Virat Kohli, the cricketer whose face sells everything from boots to broadband. At number two: Shah Rukh Khan, because of course — the man re-emerged from a five-year theatrical hiatus and promptly broke records, and the brand value never dipped for a second. And at number three, the only woman granted a standalone cover: Priyanka Chopra Jonas, who hasn't headlined a Hindi theatrical release since *The Sky Is Pink* in October 2019.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=1xjpn2KYl1M

Read that again. Seven years away from Bollywood screens, and she's still the third most commercially valuable celebrity India produces. If you want proof that the old rules — you're only as bankable as your last Friday — have quietly collapsed, this is it.

The full top ten

The complete list reads like a map of where Indian aspiration actually points: Virat Kohli, Shah Rukh Khan, Priyanka Chopra Jonas, MS Dhoni, Ranveer Singh, Akshay Kumar, Amitabh Bachchan, Sachin Tendulkar, Alia Bhatt and Allu Arjun. Four cricketers. One pan-India phenomenon in Allu Arjun, whose presence in the top ten is its own headline — a Telugu star muscling into a list long dominated by Hindi cinema and the gentlemen's game. Two women, Chopra and Bhatt. And the eternal Mr. Bachchan, still monetisable at 83.

What makes the study interesting isn't the gossip-column ranking of who's hotter than whom. It's the methodology — Interbrand brings the same brand-valuation rigour it uses on corporations to human beings, treating a celebrity like an asset class. By that cold-eyed measure, an athlete who never has a flop weekend is simply safer money than an actor who does.

The Priyanka anomaly

Nobody embodies the new logic better than Chopra Jonas. Her last Hindi film is ancient history by Bollywood's brutal clock, yet her brand has never been more global. She has been Bvlgari's Global Ambassador since 2021, became Bentley Motors' Global Ambassador in April 2026, and built a Hollywood and producing career that turned her into something bigger than any single industry — a worldwide name that Indian brands now pay a premium simply to be near.

And she isn't coasting. On the film front she's currently shooting S.S. Rajamouli's *Varanasi*, the IMAX action-adventure that has the entire industry holding its breath, playing a character named Mandakini opposite Mahesh Babu and Prithviraj Sukumaran. It's slated for a worldwide theatrical release on April 7, 2027. The desi queen who built an empire abroad is coming home on the biggest canvas Indian cinema has ever attempted.

What it means for the diaspora

For NRIs in the US, UK and Canada, this list is less surprising than it might be back home — because the diaspora has always understood star power as something bigger than the box office. The cricketer you watch at 5am on a stream, the actress who graces a Vogue cover and a Bvlgari campaign, the legend whose voice still narrates your nostalgia: brand value, to a global Indian audience, was never about the last ticket sold. It was about who you carry with you when you leave home.

That's the real takeaway from Fortune India's debut effort. The center of gravity for Indian celebrity has shifted — toward sport, toward global ambassadorships, toward stars who are valuable whether or not they're in cinemas this quarter. Movie stardom still matters enormously; SRK at number two and a Ranveer-Akshay-Bachchan run prove that. But the throne now belongs to a man with a bat, and the most valuable woman in the country built her empire while Bollywood waited. The list isn't just a ranking. It's a verdict on how fame works now.
